clue.text: Fashion short garment — it's retro but it inspires apathy

indicators.note: retro looks backwards, so everything built so far is read from right to left
something short is missing its end, so the word for the garment loses its final letter

parts.note: mode is a fashion or current style
a robe is a long loose garment

explanation.surface: A fashion editor's retro short dress leaves everyone yawning.
explanation.walkthrough: MODE plus ROB(E), the whole lot read backwards, gives BOREDOM.
explanation.definitionFit: Boredom is the weary listlessness of having nothing interesting to do, close kin to apathy.

clue.text: Researched leading basis for agent that stores energy

indicators.note: in a down clue the basis is the bottom, so this word goes below the rest
something that stores another thing keeps it inside

parts.note: James Bond, the fictional secret agent
E is the symbol for energy
a team leading is up, ahead

explanation.surface: A study of the fundamentals of a chemical that holds energy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leading' looks like 'first', but it is UP, sitting as the base under the agent.
explanation.definitionFit: To bone up is an informal phrase meaning to study or swot up on a subject.

clue.text: Go back over note on evidence

indicators.note: in a down clue a thing put on another sits above it

parts.note: re is the second note of the sol-fa scale
a trace is evidence left behind

explanation.surface: A memo is filed about some evidence in a case.
explanation.definitionFit: To retrace steps is to follow the same route again, going back along it.

clue.text: Money finally paid to you following crash

indicators.note: finally points to the end, so the last letter of each following word is taken

parts.note: the final letters of the five words

explanation.surface: Compensation at last reaches someone after a car accident.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Finally paid' looks like a single piece, but 'finally' governs all five words that follow.
explanation.definitionFit: Dough is slang for cash, as is bread.

clue.text: Gathering where nutmeg pie is shared out

indicators.note: something shared out is broken up and redistributed in new portions

parts.note: the letters of these two words

explanation.surface: At a social get-together, a spiced pie is sliced and passed round.
explanation.definitionFit: Meeting up is people coming together in one place, assembling as a group.

clue.text: Champion providing support when overwhelmed by alcohol

indicators.note: something overwhelmed is swamped and surrounded, so the support word sits inside the drink

parts.note: ale is an alcoholic drink
a post is an upright support

explanation.surface: A sportsman's backing comes with a drink problem.
explanation.definitionFit: An apostle is a zealous advocate of a cause, and a champion of a cause is one who supports it.

clue.text: A longing for what's being dropped by EastEnders

parts.note: taken as written
an itch is a restless desire

explanation.surface: Fans are desperate to know which character is being axed from the soap.
explanation.walkthrough: EastEnders is a BBC soap set in London's East End, where Cockney speech drops the H sound; aitch is the letter's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Cockneys famously leave off initial H sounds, so the letter called aitch is what they drop.

clue.text: Finished exhausted having broken the budget

parts.note: something over is finished
spent means worn out

explanation.surface: A shopper is done in and worn out after splurging past their limit.
explanation.definitionFit: To overspend is to pay out more than was allowed, exceeding a planned financial limit.

clue.text: Am I nuts travelling around in large roller?

indicators.note: travelling around moves things from place to place, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: the letters of these three words

explanation.surface: A worried traveller wonders if touring in a huge vehicle is madness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Roller' looks like a Rolls-Royce or a steamroller; here it is a rolling wave.
explanation.definitionFit: A roller is a long heavy sea wave, and a tsunami is a huge wave raised by an earthquake.

clue.text: Happen to keep it in private closet

indicators.note: keeping something means holding it within

parts.note: to ensue is to happen as a result
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone happens to keep a secret locked away in a cupboard.
explanation.walkthrough: Closet here is the old sense of water closet, a lavatory.
explanation.definitionFit: An en suite is a bathroom attached to a bedroom, a private lavatory or water closet.

clue.text: Clears this country earl to get decoration from Japan

parts.note: to net is to clear as profit
the Guardian's home country, the United Kingdom
E is an abbreviation for earl

explanation.surface: A British nobleman makes a profit and gets a Japanese honour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'This country' in a British paper means the UK.
explanation.definitionFit: A netsuke is a small carved toggle, an ornament traditionally worn on Japanese kimono sashes.

clue.text: Weather unsettled in part due to these constant movements

indicators.note: only a part of the following words is wanted, a stretch running across them

parts.note: the letters run from the end of the first word into the second

explanation.surface: Stormy weather is blamed on restless shifting air currents.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'movements' are bowel movements, not weather systems.
explanation.definitionFit: The runs is a slang term for diarrhoea, which means frequent, constant bowel movements.

clue.text: We had this out — I want an end to it

definitions.text: I want an end to it

indicators.note: having something out means thrashing it about, so these letters are thrown into disorder

parts.note: the letters of these three words

explanation.surface: After a blazing row, someone wants the argument finished for good.
explanation.definitionFit: A death wish is a desire, conscious or not, for one's own death, a wish for life to end.

clue.text: They kept tabs on everybody in almost moribund condition

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the last letter is cut off

parts.note: stasis is a state of stagnation, of no life or movement

explanation.surface: A surveillance state watched everyone while itself in terminal decline.
explanation.walkthrough: The Stasi was the East German secret police, which spied on vast numbers of citizens.
explanation.definitionFit: The East German secret police kept files on a huge share of the population, monitoring everybody.

clue.text: Media make claim of being ignored

indicators.note: words being ignored are left out, so that small word is removed from the longer one

parts.note: to profess is to claim or declare
taken as written

explanation.surface: Journalists complain that nobody pays them any attention.
explanation.walkthrough: PROFESS loses the OF from its middle to leave PRESS.
explanation.definitionFit: The press is the collective name for newspapers and journalism, the news media.

clue.text: Spooner said condition of man is at an impasse

indicators.note: Reverend Spooner swapped the opening sounds of words, so the starts of the two words trade places

parts.note: a condition is a state and a man is a male; Spooner trades their opening sounds

explanation.surface: A man's condition has reached deadlock, as the Reverend would put it.
explanation.walkthrough: Swap the starts of STATE and MALE to get STALE MATE.
explanation.definitionFit: A stalemate is a deadlock in which no progress is possible, as in chess when no legal move remains.

clue.text: Enrage VIP carved up by news network?

indicators.note: carving something up cuts it into pieces and divides it differently

parts.note: the letters of these two words

explanation.surface: A celebrity is furious at being savaged by a broadcaster.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that this network passes news informally, by gossip.
explanation.definitionFit: Hearing something on the grapevine means learning it through an informal chain of rumour and gossip.

clue.text: Faithful groom hit Canute

indicators.note: to groom is to tidy and rearrange, so the letters are reordered

parts.note: the letters of these two words

explanation.surface: A loyal servant strikes the king who tried to hold back the tide.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Faithful groom' reads as a loyal stable hand, but groom is a verb here.
explanation.definitionFit: A faithful copy is accurate and true to the original, which is to say authentic or genuine.

clue.text: Leftie gets reprimand, being where celebs parade

parts.note: a red is a left-winger
to carpet someone is to give them a dressing-down

explanation.surface: A left-wing activist gets told off at a glitzy premiere.
explanation.walkthrough: To carpet someone is British slang for calling them in to be scolded.
explanation.definitionFit: Stars walk a red carpet laid out at premieres and award ceremonies to be photographed.

clue.text: Knight turns up with extravagant oval dish

indicators.note: in a down clue, turning up means the word reads from the bottom to the top

parts.note: Sir is a knight's title
OTT is short for over the top
the letter O is oval in shape

explanation.surface: A knight arrives bearing a lavish oval serving plate.
explanation.definitionFit: Risotto is an Italian rice dish cooked slowly in stock, a dish in the sense of food served.

clue.text: Starts to use up and finish off coleslaw?

definitions.meaning: first reading: the opening letters of the last two words are two Us
second reading: the last letter of the salad word is the letter that name spells out

explanation.surface: Use up the leftovers and polish off the coleslaw.
explanation.walkthrough: Both halves describe the same letter: two Us side by side, and the final W of coleslaw, whose name is spelled out as the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The letter W is named double-u, so each description of that letter is fairly defined by its name.

clue.text: Type of charger essential to future large robots

indicators.note: what is essential lies at the heart, so the centre of each following word is taken

parts.note: the two central letters
the central letter
the two central letters

explanation.surface: Tomorrow's giant machines will rely on a powerful battery charger.
explanation.definitionFit: A turbocharger, or turbo, forces extra air into an engine; 'charger' completes the compound word.

clue.text: Call out cancelled after study

indicators.note: this word places one piece behind another in the order

parts.note: to read a subject is to study it
an event that is off has been cancelled

explanation.surface: A tutorial is scrapped once the reading is done.
explanation.definitionFit: To read off is to say aloud items from a list or a dial, announcing them one by one.

clue.text: It's curious how uneven book has everything

parts.note: odd numbers are uneven
B is an abbreviation for book
all means everything

explanation.surface: Someone remarks on how strange it is that an unbalanced book covers every topic.
explanation.definitionFit: Oddball, used as an adjective, means eccentric or strange, the same as curious in its sense of peculiar.

clue.text: Sachet occasionally filled with gold relish

indicators.note: something filled has another thing put inside it
occasionally means every so often, so only every other letter is kept

parts.note: the first, third and fifth letters
Au is the chemical symbol for gold

explanation.surface: A little packet of condiment comes stuffed with gold leaf.
explanation.definitionFit: A relish is a tangy condiment, and a sauce is likewise something served to add flavour.

clue.text: Pressurise group to make sportswear

parts.note: to sweat someone is to put pressure on them
a band is a group, of musicians for instance

explanation.surface: A coach leans on the squad to get them into kit.
explanation.definitionFit: A sweatband is a strip of towelling worn round the head or wrist by athletes, an item of sports clothing.

clue.text: Page ambassador to join group

indicators.note: joining a group here means going in among its members

parts.note: a set is a group
HE, His Excellency, is the title of an ambassador

explanation.surface: A messenger is called to join a diplomat's team.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Page' looks like a young attendant summoned to the ambassador, but it is a leaf of paper.
explanation.definitionFit: A sheet is a single leaf of paper, much as a page is.

clue.text: Send up instructions to make part of explosive

indicators.note: in a down clue, sending something up makes it read from bottom to top

parts.note: a remit is a set of instructions or terms of reference

explanation.surface: Orders are passed upwards on how to build a bomb.
explanation.definitionFit: A timer is the clock component of a time bomb, the piece that sets off the detonation.

clue.text: Cultivated place for money holder generation

parts.note: a till is a cash register
an age is a generation or era

explanation.surface: A cash register belongs to a whole era of shopkeeping.
explanation.definitionFit: Tillage is land that has been ploughed and prepared for crops, ground under cultivation.

clue.text: Device storing large amount of data — and a game!

indicators.note: a thing storing something holds it inside

parts.note: a tool is a device or implement
MB is a megabyte
taken as written

explanation.surface: A gadget with plenty of memory doubles as entertainment.
explanation.walkthrough: A tombola is a raffle-style lottery played at British fêtes, prizes drawn from a revolving drum.
explanation.definitionFit: A tombola is a game of chance in which numbered tickets are drawn to win prizes.

clue.text: Work university advanced is magnificent

parts.note: op is short for opus, a work
U is the abbreviation for university
advanced money is lent

explanation.surface: A grant paid upfront to a university project turns out splendid.
explanation.definitionFit: Opulent describes lavish richness and splendour, the sort of grandeur meant by magnificent.

clue.text: Beware occupants of packed vehicle carrying drug

definitions.note: imperative verb; the answer is the exclamation 'Careful!'

indicators.note: a vehicle carrying something has it on board, inside

parts.note: as many people as a car will hold
E is ecstasy

explanation.surface: A warning to watch out for a car crammed with smugglers.
explanation.definitionFit: Shouting 'Careful!' is a warning to take heed, just as 'Beware!' is.
